$comment: Sourced local facts for the city pages. Every value carries source ids (see "sources") and a confidence. scripts/migrate/content/local-facts.mjs writes only confidence "high" values to the location documents. Neighborhoods are only names the business already uses in its own copy (homepage tiles or the location body); each carries the quote that names it, which the module checks. Human-readable version: docs/research/local-facts.md.

method.zipCodes: Census 2020 ZCTA-to-place relationship file: a ZIP is listed when at least 40% of its land is inside the city limits, or it covers at least 5% of the city’s land (and at least 0.25 sq mi of overlap). ZIPs under 50% are listed in "partlyInCity". ZCTAs approximate USPS ZIP areas; USPS lookups were not reachable (bot protection), so USPS city names were not checked.
method.geo: USGS GNIS populated-place point (traditional town center), rounded to 4 decimals. Census 2025 Gazetteer internal points were used as a cross-check.
method.utilityProviders: Values use the schema list (SRP, APS, City of Mesa, TEP, ED3). Boundaries from SRP’s 2026 Electric Service Specifications map (which draws the APS pockets inside SRP’s area) and APS’s Metro Phoenix territory map, plus each city’s own utility listing where reachable. Utility territory is set by address; nuance goes in "detail" and permitNotes.
method.permitAuthority: Official city/town/county pages. Several city sites (mesaaz.gov, gilbertaz.gov, tempe.gov, queencreekaz.gov, explore.pinal.gov, azmag.gov) return 403 to automated fetches; their content was confirmed through search-engine extracts of the official pages and is marked in the source note.

quotes: Contact both SRP and the AHJ prior to making any panel modifications and/or repair to an existing service entrance section. SRP will reconnect power when both SRP and the AHJ approve all service entrance section modifications.

Maricopa County and most cities/towns in SRP’s service area have ordinances restricting SRP from energizing the load side of the electrical service to the Customer until the Customer has obtained the necessary permits and until the actual electrical installation has been approved by the AHJ.

value: Residential electrical permits in Mesa are issued by the City of Mesa Development Services Department, which handles plan review, permits and inspections. Installing or modifying electrical systems is on the city’s list of work that needs a construction permit.

Mesa has two electric utilities: the City of Mesa serves a 5.5-square-mile area centered on downtown, and SRP serves the rest of the city. In SRP’s area, SRP’s service specifications say to contact both SRP and the permitting authority before a panel upgrade, and SRP reconnects power once both approve the work.
